name: Beach / Coastal Camping
tagline: For campers pitching on sand or just above the shore at a seashore campground or wilderness beach.
description: A starting point for 1-4 nights at a coastal campground or beach site, car-accessible or a short walk in. Assumes wind, salt, sand, strong sun, biting insects, and tides that change where you can safely camp. Adapt for wilderness coasts (permits, bear canisters, headland tide timing) versus developed seashores (reservations, beach-driving permits), and for cold-water versus hot-weather coasts.
considerations: Check NOAA tide predictions and the marine forecast; camp well above the highest high tide and expect storms and wave setup to push water higher.
Check current permit rules: wilderness coasts often require permits and bear canisters, and some seashores require beach-driving permits.
Check current fire rules; many beaches allow fires only below the high-tide line or ban them seasonally.
Expect wind: bring a sturdy tent, long sand stakes, and guy everything out.
Biting insects (mosquitoes, flies, no-see-ums, ticks) can be severe; bring repellent and screens.
Check drinking-water availability; many beach sites have none.

items.text: Tide table for your beach saved or printed, with high-tide times noted
items.note: Use NOAA tide predictions; a storm can push water well above the predicted level.

items.text: Marine and weather forecast: wind, surf, storms
Campsite reservation or wilderness permit where required
items.note: Check current rules; some seashores need no permit but charge entrance fees.

items.text: Trip plan shared with someone
Fire rules checked (location, size, seasonal bans)
Beach-driving (ORV) permit if driving on sand
Map with headlands and escape routes marked (wilderness coast)
items.note: Round headlands only at the tide levels the map shows as safe.

items.text: Sturdy wind-rated tent with full rainfly
Sand stakes (12 in or longer, or corkscrew) or buried deadman anchors
Extra guylines, with every guy-out used
Sleeping bag (coastal nights are damp and cool)
Sleeping pad
Groundsheet or footprint
Shade canopy or screen tent with sand anchors
Pillows
Tarp or mat at the door for de-sanding feet
Dustpan and brush
Drinking water: 1 gallon or more per person per day (many beaches have none)
Water containers and bottles
Stove and fuel (fires may be banned or limited to below the tide line)
Lighter and matches in a waterproof container
Cookware, utensils, and dishes
Cooler with ice, food in sealed containers
Trash bags; pack out everything, no burying
Windscreen for the stove
Water filter (only if fresh sources exist; iodine alone misses crypto)
Bear canister (required on some wilderness coasts; also stops raccoons)
items.note: Check current food-storage rules for the beach you are visiting.

items.text: Wash bins and biodegradable soap
Sun hat and sunglasses
Sun shirt or rash guard and long pants
Windbreaker or rain jacket
Warm layers for evening: fleece and beanie
Water shoes or sandals with heel straps
Swimsuit and quick-dry towel
Spare dry clothes in a dry bag
Light long-sleeve layer for bugs at dusk
Sunscreen SPF 30+ (reapply) and lip balm
Insect repellent plus a head net
First-aid kit with tweezers, antihistamine, and blister care
Headlamp or flashlight with spare batteries
Knife or multi-tool
Whistle
Emergency blanket
Phone and battery bank; satellite messenger on wilderness coasts
Life jackets for kids and paddling; know rip-current safety
Toilet paper and hand sanitizer
WAG bags or portable toilet where there are no toilets
items.note: Sand catholes get exposed; many beaches require packing out human waste.

items.text: Trowel (intertidal catholes allowed on some wilderness coasts)
Toothbrush and toothpaste
Fresh-water rinse jug or solar shower
Baby powder (removes sand from skin)
Mallet for stakes
Duct tape, cord, and tent repair kit
Shovel (anchors, fire pit, vehicle recovery)
Traction boards, tire gauge, and compressor if driving on sand
Dry bags for electronics
Beach toys and frisbee
Binoculars and field guide (birds, tide pools)
Low-profile camp chairs
Firewood bought locally or gathered from the beach only where allowed
